heading: Introduction & The Range of Rhetoric (Opening)
outline: Introduction: identification vs. persuasion; intermediate rhetorical area; range from propaganda to pure persuasion
The Use of Milton's Samson: layered identification (Milton/Samson/God; Puritan/Israelite); literature for use at one remove; 'substantially' saying
Qualifying the Suicidal Motive: motivational recipe vs. gist reduction; dramatic subterfuge; context-as-qualifier
Self-Immolation in Matthew Arnold: Empedocles/Sohrab as variants of one attitudinal cluster; inter-work identification; pious self-abnegation toward the father
The Imaging of Transformation: murder/suicide as convertible terms; ground-motive of transformation; catalogue of transformation-images
Dramatic and Philosophic Terms for Essence: entelechy as philosophic essence-by-culmination; death as transfiguration; temporizing of essence (culminative pole)
'Tragic' Terms for Personality Types: neotragic eschatological classification; scene-agent ratio; cross-reference to Grammar pp. 7–9
Imagery at Face Value: adolescent violence-imagery as transformation-vocabulary; absence of formal distancing in photographic art; critique of reductive psychoanalysis

concepts.label: Identification
concepts.gloss: The book's master rhetorical term, here enacted through Milton/Samson, Arnold/Empedocles, faction/biblical-figure structures before receiving formal definition at p.19. The motive-structure by which separate entities are rendered consubstantial.

concepts.label: Consubstantiality (implicit)
concepts.gloss: Not yet named but enacted throughout: Milton's 'substantially' saying, Arnold's two poems sharing the one authorship's substance, faction sharing biblical substance. The formal term is deferred to RM-01.

concepts.label: Imaging of Transformation
concepts.gloss: Transformation is the ground-motive; killing/suicide/self-immolation are one family of available images for localizing it. Includes Upward/Downward Way, Exile/Homecoming, seasonal cycles, Day/Night antitheses as equally valid alternatives.

concepts.label: Terministic Screen (implicit)
concepts.gloss: Not yet named, but the logic is fully operational: the specific transformation-image chosen screens what motivational dimensions appear (Milton's theocratic terms screen the suicidal; Arnold's lyric softness screens the martial).

concepts.label: Dramatic Terms for Essence
concepts.gloss: Narrative/temporal translation of philosophical essence-claims: the end of a story formally declares the protagonist's essential character. Opposed to philosophic terms; convertible with them by heuristic reversal.

concepts.label: Philosophic Terms for Essence
concepts.gloss: Abstract, timeless characterizations of a kind's perfection (e.g., 'rational animal'). Conceals a temporal logic (finishedness = end) making it convertible with the dramatic/narrative form.

concepts.label: Entelechy (Aristotelian)
concepts.gloss: Classifying a kind by the perfection of which it is capable; the philosophic form of 'essence-by-culmination.' Its narrative translation is 'death as transfiguration' — the tragic dignifying of a motive.

concepts.label: Temporizing of Essence
concepts.gloss: Cross-reference to Grammar pp.430–440. Logical essence expressed in temporal/narrative form: either as origin (ancestral) or as culmination (culminative — the pole RM-00 adds). Both poles personalize essence.

concepts.label: Suicidal Motive
concepts.gloss: Reflexive form of the death-motive, fusing agency and passivity in one figure. Requires contextual qualification; when stripped of its modifiers by reductive reading it becomes 'efficient' — purely suicidal.

concepts.label: Motivational Recipe
concepts.gloss: The total complex of motivational ingredients in their proportions and contextual qualifications. Cannot be reduced to a single 'gist' without misrepresenting the whole; the metaphor captures compositional logic.

concepts.label: Intermediate Rhetorical Area
concepts.gloss: The domain between fully deliberate intent and fully unconscious expression — rhetoric's proper home. The politician who may be sincerely self-deceived inhabits it. Classical 'persuasion' cannot capture it; 'identification' can.

concepts.label: Scene-Agent Ratio
concepts.gloss: Cross-reference to Grammar pp.7–9. The formal ratio by which a person's character and their surrounding scene's character are identified with each other; enables self-transcendence through scale-shift (personal → cosmic).

concepts.label: Literature for Use
concepts.gloss: Literary works performing rhetorical-political work: overtly (Areopagitica) or at one remove (Samson — ritual and magic order). Anticipates the Introduction's range from propaganda to pure persuasion.

concepts.label: Dramatic Subterfuge
concepts.gloss: The mechanism by which dramatic form allows inclusion of motivational ingredients inadmissible in analytic form. Milton's theocratic mission admits the suicidal strand; stated analytically, it would be impermissible.

concepts.label: Imagery at Face Value
concepts.gloss: The interpretive stance of accepting imagery on its own terms as having real rhetorical effect, without psychoanalytic reduction to an unconscious 'gist.' Imagery shapes motivation and cannot be neutralized by declaring it merely symbolic.

concepts.label: Persuasion (Range of)
concepts.gloss: The full spectrum from bluntest propaganda through courtship, etiquette, education, sermon to 'pure persuasion' — appeal enjoyed for its own sake. Demonstrates why 'persuasion' alone is too narrow a master term.

concepts.label: Inter-Work Identification
concepts.gloss: Author's consubstantiality across texts: Arnold's two poems share the common substance of one authorship, making both expressions of the same attitudinal cluster. Demonstrates identification across works, not only within them.

positions.claim: Identification, not persuasion, is the more capacious master term for rhetoric, capable of capturing the intermediate area of expression that is neither wholly deliberate nor wholly unconscious.
A motivational recipe cannot be justly reduced to a single 'gist' ingredient; the qualifying modifiers supplied by dramatic context are themselves constitutive of the motive as a whole.

Imagery of killing, suicide, and self-immolation is one terminological family among many for localizing the process of transformation in general; the specific family chosen reveals motivational character, not a direct 'desire to kill.'

Dramatic terms for essence (the end of a narrative as formal proclamation of essence) and philosophic terms for essence (entelechy, abstract finishedness) are formally homologous and mutually convertible by heuristic reversal.

Imagery taken at face value performs real rhetorical work on motivation; it cannot be neutralized by declaring it 'merely symbolic,' and the absence of formal distancing devices (as in photographic realism) intensifies its motivational effect.

calleja_pim_candidates.rationale: Imaging-of-transformation analysis shows that players use game-imagery as a vocabulary for self-change narrative, paralleling how poets localize the transformation-process through available imagery families.

Face-value imagery analysis: game imagery at face value shapes player motivation and attitudinal orientation; cannot be reduced to 'unconscious' drives. Culminative essence-definition maps to the affective charge of player-identity moments.
Scene-agent ratio: the character of a game-world scene and the character of the player are identified with each other; player choice of game-world type reveals motivational orientation.

Factional identification (Puritan/Israelite, Royalist/Philistine) anticipates guild/team/faction identification in multiplayer games; group identity through consubstantiation with a collective symbol.

tensions.description: Face value vs. reduction: taking imagery on its own terms (full motivational recipe) vs. reducing it to a gist motive (psychoanalytic 'desire to kill'). Burke sides with face value but must account for when gist-reduction does identify a real motivational strand.

Dramatic vs. philosophic terms for essence: narrative culmination vs. abstract timeless classification. Burke shows they are formally homologous and convertible, but the tension between temporal and timeless modes of essence-statement is not fully resolved — it persists as an analytic resource.

Identification as positive binding force vs. identification as vehicle for enslavement and obstinacy (Milton's 'cantankerous old fighter-priest'). Blum's formulation captures both; RM-00 shows that the same identificatory move can generate cooperation or fanaticism depending on the motivational recipe.
